bull_bear.body: Revenue per employee jumped to $75k (from $56k 3 years ago) driven by AI + outcome pricing, not just offshoring; 'Agency-of-Record' pilot reduced creative cycle from 3 months to 3 days using synthetic KOLs and agentic workflows; TCPA lawsuit stems from FY19-20 fax usage (now inactive channel); DSO improved to 63 days (from 72), driving record cash flows despite M&A outflows.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net cash position of INR 14,602 Mn at 30 June 2026 (including cash and cash equivalents, current investments, bank balances and non-current bank deposits), down from 15,385 Mn at Mar-2026 and 17,280 Mn a year earlier.
- Working capital: Net DSO (Billed + Unbilled - Unearned) at 67 days, four days worse QoQ (63 at Mar-2026) but four days better YoY (71).
- The deck makes no statement on dividend, buyback, acquisitions or capex allocation - reinvestment is described only qualitatively as "investments in strengthening our sales and go-to-market teams last year" and investments "made ahead of curve" now converting to revenue.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Nearly three decades (27+ years) of exclusive focus on a single industry - life sciences - creating domain depth that generic technology firms and horizontal outsourcers cannot match
- Serves all 20 of the world's top 20 biopharma companies and 80 of the top 100, with over 8 years of executive relationships across the top 20
- Proprietary life sciences-native AI operating system: an intelligent data layer built on more than three million HCP engagement signals and two decades of commercial content and taxonomies, plus the Cortex reasoning engine and a Mesh of production AI agents
- Embedded in client revenue - the Company supports commercial and medical workflows tied to product launches and brand performance, so client spend grows with client revenue rather than with cost-cutting cycles
- Outcome-aligned engagement model: a substantial and growing proportion of revenues are output-based or catalog-priced rather than FTE-based, letting efficiency gains accrue to margin instead of per-headcount rate erosion
- Net revenue retention above 100% for the last five years, evidencing switching costs and account expansion
- Displaces fragmented agency and CRO wallets rather than competing for the horizontal IT dollar, giving a materially larger and less contested opportunity set
- Scale credentials: 3M+ HCPs digitally profiled and engaged, 800+ brands activated, 100+ product launches supported, 65,000 MLR assets reviewed since 2015 and 7,000+ labels managed at 99.5% first-time-right
- Talent mix blending science and technology - over 27% of employees are healthcare experts (more than 1,500 life sciences specialists) and 25% are technology and AI experts
- CMMI Level 5 process maturity supporting predictable, statistically managed delivery
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Client concentration in a narrow set of global biopharma buyers — 58.5% of revenues are derived from the top 20 global biopharma companies, and the client base is only 91 active clients; a budget cut, vendor consolidation or loss at one or two large accounts would be disproportionately felt.
- Dependence on global life sciences industry operating spend — The Company states its revenue performance is closely aligned with global life sciences industry spending on operations, so the top line moves with client commercialization budgets rather than with an independent demand cycle.
- Pharma patent cliff and loss of exclusivity by 2030 — A wave of blockbuster patent expiries exposes clients to generic and biosimilar competition on a scale rarely seen, pressuring the commercial budgets that Indegene's work is embedded in - even as it also creates the modernization demand the Company sells into.
- Technology / AI disruption of the work Indegene itself performs — The Company's thesis is that generic foundation models cannot reason about regulated life sciences workflows; if that domain moat narrows, or if clients build in-house, the pricing power of an outcome-based model built on AI-driven efficiency erodes. Management explicitly ties competitiveness to embedding AI faster than the industry.
- Data privacy, PII handling and information security across regulated client workflows — The business processes HCP and patient-linked data in regulated environments; risk management is built around privacy impact assessments (PIA/DPIA), PII asset and data-flow registers, Records of Processing Activities, an enterprise-wide network of Privacy Champions and continuous security-awareness and phishing-resilience programs, indicating the exposure is treated as material.
- Third-party and vendor dependency — A structured Third-Party Risk Management programme aligned to ISO/IEC 27036, ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 31000 governs the vendor lifecycle - reflecting reliance on external technology, data-subscription and delivery partners in an accountable, regulated delivery chain.
- Talent attrition and dependence on scarce domain-plus-AI specialists — Delivery rests on over 5,500 professionals including more than 1,500 life sciences specialists; voluntary turnover for permanent employees was 16.35% in FY 2025-26 (17.13% in FY 2024-25), and the judgement-intensive work cannot be staffed generically.
- Near-total export revenue concentration and cross-border regulatory exposure — Exports contributed 98.47% of turnover in FY 2025-26 (98.27% in FY 2024-25, including inter-company revenue), leaving earnings exposed to currency movements, cross-border tax/regulatory change and client-country policy shifts.
- Climate change and GHG emissions as an ESG-linked commercial risk — Identified in the BRSR as a material issue: although a digital-first services company has a lower direct footprint, office operations, purchased electricity, business travel and cloud/data-centre usage plus rising climate expectations from global life sciences clients mean failure to monitor and reduce emissions could affect client expectations, ESG ratings, competitiveness in ESG-sensitive client bids and regulatory preparedness.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Explicitly rejects peer categories - "We don't fit the IT-services, Agency or CRO box" and "Indegene is a new category - not a better version of an old one" - built on a four-part EDGE frame: Embedded Revenue Partner, Deep Domain Expertise, GenAI Disruptor, Engagement Model.
- "Embedded Revenue Partner": operates in clients' revenue-generating engine (Commercial & Med teams behind launches, brands & growth) and sits "on growth-side budgets, not IT cost budgets; less exposed to cost-cutting cycles".
- Deep domain moat: "over 27 years of experience in life sciences", deeply integrated in client workflows managing "critical workflows requiring high degree of domain expertise and regulatory compliance" - "Judgment-intensive work where GenAI compounds domain knowledge rather than replacing it"; 29%+ of delivery employees from healthcare backgrounds.
- Positions GenAI deflation as an advantage, not a threat: "GenAI price deflation pressures large incumbents but provides growth headroom for us at our current scale", with AI-enabled solutions engaging "at enterprise level (not brand-by-brand)" to take "wallet share from incumbents".
- Operates "at the intersection of healthcare and technology", pairing Healthcare Expertise (market understanding, regulatory navigation, medical content know-how) with Tech-Led Delivery (digital-first, GenAI tools and platforms, advanced analytics).

business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Indegene helps biopharma, emerging biotech and medical technology companies modernize and scale commercialization operations across five core pillars - Discovery & Evidence, Regulatory & Compliance, Commercial Launch, Content & Engagement, and Patient & Outcomes - combining deep life sciences domain expertise with AI-embedded platforms and governed operating models. The Company positions itself as neither a life sciences IT company, a horizontal outsourcer, a specialty agency nor a CRO, but as a domain-deep platform that takes accountability for regulated workflows and the business outcomes they deliver. As of March 31, 2026 it served all of the world's top 20 biopharma companies and 91 active clients, operating in more than 80 markets through 17+ delivery and operational centers across 11 countries with over 5,500 professionals.
business.title: What they do

business.body:

- **Next-generation AI-embedded operating models:** One-Click Submission, Agentic AOR (Agency of Record) of the Future, Safety-in-a-Box, AI-powered Personalized Customer Engagement, Intelligent Clinical Trial Operations, Tectonic (GenAI-embedded 'agency-of-scale' model for creative development, adaptation and execution)
- **Service lines:** Commercial, Medical, R&D, Safety, AI & Platforms
- **Business lines:** Enterprise Commercial, Enterprise Medical

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Position as the 'strategic operating partner' / AI-Native Life Sciences Operating Partner - a new category distinct from consulting without execution, horizontal IT/system integration without domain depth, specialty agencies and CROs - by combining consulting, purpose-built technology platforms, deep life sciences expertise and global execution.
- Stay exclusively focused on one industry (life sciences) and treat that single-industry depth, built over nearly three decades, as the core differentiator that makes AI work where generic models do not.
- Deepen strategic client relationships through integrated enterprise operating models - expanding wallet share across existing clients and broadening enterprise engagements across functions, geographies and brands.
- Continue investing in AI, proprietary platforms (Cortex intelligence layer and the fabric of AI agents built on it), domain expertise and consulting capabilities.
- Expand market presence across therapeutic areas and geographies while selectively extending capabilities through strategic, capability-led acquisitions.
- Scale AI-embedded operating models that modernize clients' commercial, medical, regulatory and clinical functions - redesigning operating models around AI rather than merely adopting AI.
- Run an outcome-aligned engagement model anchored on outputs and outcomes rather than FTE staffing, with a substantial and growing proportion of revenues output-based or catalog-priced so efficiency gains accrue to margin rather than to per-headcount rate erosion.
- Displace fragmented agency and CRO wallets rather than compete for the horizontal IT dollar, operating in a materially larger and less contested opportunity set.
- Keep human judgment central - design human centrality into every operating model, with AI amplifying rather than replacing domain depth.
- Invest in people as an AI-native workforce, building careers at the intersection of domain depth, AI fluency and outcome ownership.
- Anchor CSR on strengthening India's deep science ecosystem - accelerating lab-to-market translation, interdisciplinary research excellence and enabling policy - alongside elite sport, palliative care, foundational education and school nutrition.
- The Board's stated remit includes developing strategy, overseeing material acquisitions and divestments, managing capital expenditure and the Company's capital structure, and handling other financing matters. A Board-constituted Investment Committee - chaired by an Independent Director and comprising three independent and two non-executive directors as on 31 March 2026 - reviews and evaluates proposals for investment (including acquisitions), divestments, strategic alliances and technological tie-ups, and large projects requiring capital expenditure based on the strategic plans of the Company or its subsidiaries, making recommendations to the Board; it also reviews post-transaction completion and integration against acquisition plans. On distributions, the Board has recommended a final dividend on equity shares for the financial year ended 31 March 2026 for members' approval at the 28th Annual General Meeting (13 August 2026). No formal dividend-payout, buyback or leverage policy is articulated in the routed text.
- Establish and maintain a GHG inventory covering Scope 1, Scope 2 and relevant Scope 3 categories, monitoring electricity and business-travel emissions and engaging cloud/data-centre and key service providers on emissions performance.
- Integrate climate-related considerations into enterprise risk management and business continuity planning, with ESG and BRSR considerations embedded directly in the enterprise risk taxonomy.
- Procure renewable energy through wheeling arrangements and Power Purchase Agreements wherever feasible.
- Reduce dependence on physical data centres by transitioning to cloud-based infrastructure and co-located data centres, with thermal management (cold/hot aisle separation, blanking panels) and ASHRAE-aligned practices in data-centre operations.
- Progressive energy-efficiency programme across green and existing buildings - sensor-based LED lighting transition, Energy Star-rated and energy-efficient equipment, optimised HVAC operations and replacement of inefficient equipment - supported by formal energy management practices and employee awareness initiatives.
- Obtain external assurance on BRSR core indicators - reasonable assurance as per ISAE 3000 carried out by TUV SUD South Asia Pvt. Ltd. for FY 2025-26.
- Report annually under the BRSR framework aligned to the nine NGRBC principles and Regulation 34(2)(f) of the SEBI Listing Regulations, with enhanced disclosures and improved alignment of ESG priorities to business strategy year over year.
- Maintain gender-balanced workforce participation - women were 44.48% of permanent employees, 18.18% of the Board of Directors and 25.00% of Key Management Personnel as of 31 March 2026.
- Operate grievance-redressal mechanisms across all stakeholder groups (whistleblower and investor-grievance channels), with nil complaints filed and nil pending across NGRBC principles in FY 2025-26.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Indegene's expansion is capability- and footprint-led rather than plant-and-machinery led. During FY 2025-26 the Company completed three strategic acquisitions to strengthen capabilities and expand presence in key geographies. BioPharm, acquired in October 2025, strengthened omnichannel data and targeting capabilities within the enterprise commercial segment through the addition of the Tandem data platform; its integration was completed ahead of schedule by the end of February 2026, with synergies on general and administrative expense, data subscriptions, business operations and go-to-market progressively unlocking through FY 2026-27. Alongside BioPharm, the Company acquired Warn & Co and Cake Kommunikations - additions of people with deep expertise and local market knowledge in key European geographies that complement the global delivery model in Europe with on-the-ground credibility and relationships. Physical footprint expansion has been through global delivery centers: new centers opened in London, Pune and Mumbai, a new global delivery center in Noida, an earlier delivery center in Hyderabad, a strategic center in Germany, a new entity launched in Spain and a China operation center at Shanghai and Dalian - taking the network to 17+ delivery and operational centers across 11 countries serving more than 80 markets, supported by hubs and offices across North America, Europe and Asia. The Company also continued to invest in senior leadership and thought-leadership talent across commercial and medical leadership to engage at C-suite level for larger transformation mandates, and in building and scaling category-defining technology platforms and GenAI-embedded solutions (Cortex and the solutions built on it). Forward capex/expansion intent stated in the Business Outlook is to keep investing in AI, proprietary platforms, domain expertise and consulting capabilities, and to expand across therapeutic areas and geographies while selectively pursuing capability-led acquisitions. No rupee capex budget, plant capacity or commissioning schedule is disclosed.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global pharma revenues are projected to grow to nearly $2 trillion by 2030, propelled by ageing populations, rising chronic and complex disease burden, expanding emerging-market access and innovation across biologics, cell and gene therapies and precision medicine.
- Pharma companies invest more than $500 billion annually across research, development and commercialization, and 50-55 Novel Active Substances are expected to launch annually in the United States through 2030, led by oncology, immunology and rare disease specialty therapies.
- An approaching wave of patent expiries, with blockbuster products losing exclusivity by 2030, widens the gap between scientific promise and commercial-engine performance and forces clients to re-architect how products move from lab to patient.
- Clients are shifting from isolated AI pilots to embedding AI into the core operating fabric of commercialization - running trials faster, preparing submissions in days rather than months, keeping content compliant at scale and engaging HCPs through intelligent omnichannel experiences.
- The industry is converging on a new kind of partner that can own outcomes across the value chain rather than merely advise - described as a large and expanding addressable opportunity for Indegene.
- Revenue performance is closely aligned with global life sciences industry spending on operations, with 58.5% of revenues derived from the top 20 global biopharma companies.
- Client spend is embedded in client revenue rather than in cost-cutting cycles, because Indegene supports commercial and medical workflows tied to product launches, brand performance and market growth.
- Operating leverage: revenue has continued to grow several times faster than headcount as AI is embedded more deeply into delivery, with efficiency gains accruing to margin under an output-based / catalog-priced model.
- Growth is being driven by enterprise-wide transformation programs spanning functions, brands and markets, where activities that once took weeks can be completed in hours.
- Next-generation operating models already in production - regulatory pathways compressed from months to weeks, medico-legal review re-engineered for sub-24-hour turnaround, agentic content operations collapsing creative cycles from months to days, and real-time adaptive omnichannel engagement.
- No order book or backlog figure is disclosed in the routed text; the Company points to net revenue retention consistently above 100% for the last five years as evidence of expanding strategic relationships.
- Increasingly partnering on enterprise-wide transformation programs spanning functions, brands and markets, producing deep multi-year engagements and compounding long-term opportunities.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Indegene crossed ₹1,000cr quarterly revenue for the first time, driven by GenAI-enabled outcome contracts and deepening top-20 pharma relationships, while reported PAT dipped due to a one-time legal provision and forex hedge accounting changes. The strategic pivot from 'IT services' to 'strategic operating partner' is validating via multi-year deals (Tectonic, Omnichannel) that shift spend from agencies/CROs to Indegene, setting up margin recovery and accelerated growth in FY27.

open.item: Synergies from the BioPharm acquisition on general and administrative expense, data subscriptions, business operations and go-to-market are to progressively unlock through FY 2026-27, with integration already completed ahead of schedule by end-February 2026.

Management states the pipeline entering FY 2026-27 is stronger and larger than at any prior year-end, with breadth across top-20 customers, the outside-top-20 cohort and both Enterprise Commercial and Enterprise Medical business lines.
Continue investing in and scaling category-defining technology platforms and GenAI-embedded solutions, plus senior leadership talent, to sustain the growth journey during FY 2026-27.
Deepen strategic client relationships by expanding enterprise engagements, increasing revenue share and supporting more functions across the commercialization lifecycle.
Continue investing in AI, proprietary platforms, domain expertise and consulting capabilities to strengthen the Company's differentiated offerings.
Expand market presence across therapeutic areas and geographies while selectively pursuing acquisitions that strengthen capabilities and reach.
Scale AI-embedded operating models that help clients modernize commercial, medical, regulatory and clinical functions with greater speed, quality and efficiency.
Selectively extend capabilities through strategic, capability-led acquisitions while expanding market presence across therapeutic areas and geographies.

drhp.one_liner: Indegene Limited is the AI-native strategic operating partner to the global life sciences industry, designing and running the regulated commercial, medical, regulatory, safety and clinical workflows that move a molecule from laboratory to launch to the millionth patient prescription.

plants.capacity: 17+ delivery and operational centers across 11 countries; presence in 80+ markets
plants.role: Hubs and offices across North America, Europe and Asia supporting a globally distributed delivery model

AI platforms and data layer: Cortex (life sciences-native, LLM-agnostic reasoning engine encoding domain expertise in semantic knowledge graphs)
Mesh of expert AI agents (creative content, medical writing, medico-legal review, safety monitoring, HCP journey optimization, submissions planning)
Cockpit of domain experts orchestrating regulated workflows
Tandem data platform (added through the BioPharm acquisition)
Next-generation AI-embedded operating mo: Agentic AOR (Agency of Record) of the Future
Tectonic (GenAI-embedded 'agency-of-scale' model for creative development, adaptation and execution)

risks.note: 58.5% of revenues are derived from the top 20 global biopharma companies, and the client base is only 91 active clients; a budget cut, vendor consolidation or loss at one or two large accounts would be disproportionately felt.
risks.risk: Client concentration in a narrow set of global biopharma buyers

risks.note: The Company states its revenue performance is closely aligned with global life sciences industry spending on operations, so the top line moves with client commercialization budgets rather than with an independent demand cycle.
risks.risk: Dependence on global life sciences industry operating spend

risks.note: A wave of blockbuster patent expiries exposes clients to generic and biosimilar competition on a scale rarely seen, pressuring the commercial budgets that Indegene's work is embedded in - even as it also creates the modernization demand the Company sells into.
risks.risk: Pharma patent cliff and loss of exclusivity by 2030

risks.note: The Company's thesis is that generic foundation models cannot reason about regulated life sciences workflows; if that domain moat narrows, or if clients build in-house, the pricing power of an outcome-based model built on AI-driven efficiency erodes. Management explicitly ties competitiveness to embedding AI faster than the industry.
risks.risk: Technology / AI disruption of the work Indegene itself performs

risks.note: The business processes HCP and patient-linked data in regulated environments; risk management is built around privacy impact assessments (PIA/DPIA), PII asset and data-flow registers, Records of Processing Activities, an enterprise-wide network of Privacy Champions and continuous security-awareness and phishing-resilience programs, indicating the exposure is treated as material.
risks.risk: Data privacy, PII handling and information security across regulated client workflows

risks.note: A structured Third-Party Risk Management programme aligned to ISO/IEC 27036, ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 31000 governs the vendor lifecycle - reflecting reliance on external technology, data-subscription and delivery partners in an accountable, regulated delivery chain.

Delivery rests on over 5,500 professionals including more than 1,500 life sciences specialists; voluntary turnover for permanent employees was 16.35% in FY 2025-26 (17.13% in FY 2024-25), and the judgement-intensive work cannot be staffed generically.
risks.risk: Talent attrition and dependence on scarce domain-plus-AI specialists

risks.note: Exports contributed 98.47% of turnover in FY 2025-26 (98.27% in FY 2024-25, including inter-company revenue), leaving earnings exposed to currency movements, cross-border tax/regulatory change and client-country policy shifts.
risks.risk: Near-total export revenue concentration and cross-border regulatory exposure
